headline.question: How healthy is Canada's labour market?
headline.label: unemployment rate

changes: The unemployment rate rose 0.2 points to 6.7% in October 2026. Pushed it up: job losses +0.02, population growth +0.08, participation in job market +0.04.
Employment fell by 5k in October (full-time −18k, part-time +13k); over the past 12 months it rose by 16k.
There were 2.9 unemployed people for every job vacancy in August 2026 (3.3 a year earlier), and 23.7% of unemployed people had been looking for over 6 months (22.3% a year earlier).
Against their own history since 2000, 15 to 24 year olds with a bachelor's degree are the worst off: 9.3% unemployed (12-month average), the 84th percentile.
Average hourly wages were up 2.3% on a year earlier and consumer prices 3.1% (September 2026): real wages down 0.8%.

charts.title: Are people staying unemployed longer?
charts.reading: In October 2026, 23.7% of unemployed people had been looking for over 6 months, and 13.0% for over a year.

charts.title: Which groups are worse off than usual?
charts.reading: All ages and education levels: 6.7% unemployed, the 33rd percentile of its history since 2000. Furthest above normal: 15 to 24 year olds with high school or less (84th) and with a bachelor's degree (84th).
charts.note: Unemployment rate by age and education, 12-month average to October 2026, not seasonally adjusted; percentile against each group's own history since January 2000.

charts.title: How unusual has each group's unemployment been?
charts.reading: In June 2021, all 15 groups were at the 75th percentile or above, the most since 2000; in October 2026, 4 are.
charts.note: Each group's 12-month average unemployment rate as a percentile of its own history since January 2000; not seasonally adjusted.
